decisions.statement: A line continuation is joined before the line is cut.
A quoted run with one bare word is unquoted before the cut.
Every other quoted run is taken out before the cut.
A newline cuts as a separator does.
The body a heredoc has is written rather than run.
A body is taken out from the line opening that body to the line ending that body.
The line opening a body is kept.
A redirect on the line opening a body is read.
A body opening a heredoc of its own opens nothing.
An opening the text never ends takes no line out.
A herestring opens no body.
Every separator form cuts too.
An empty segment is dropped.
Leading space is taken off the ones kept.
A word is matched by its basename.
A prefix that only runs the call behind the prefix is stepped over.
A prefix's own flags are stepped over with the prefix.
A prefix flag taking a value takes the word after that flag.
A prefix takes the numbers the prefix is named as taking and no other word.
A prefix flag that asks rather than runs leaves no call.
A prefix behind a prefix is stepped over too.
A variable assignment before a call is stepped over.
The text is cut here rather than read for the text's meaning.
No tool a hook guards is named here.
This module reads a shell command line without being a shell.
A shell marks no word as a word that runs the call behind that word.
Every hook cuts a command line the same way without saying how twice.
A prefix this module does not name hides the call behind that prefix from every hook.
An assignment whose value the shell rewrites hides the call in that value from every hook.
A substitution in command position is read as part of the command word.
A subshell's opening parenthesis is read as part of the command word.
A variable in command position is read as that variable rather than its value.
A double-quoted substitution is taken out whole, leaving the line no segment.
A call a substitution, a subshell or a variable holds is found as a call on the line is.
A call a prefix or an assignment's value holds is found as a call on the line is.

definition: a shell command line cut into the segments and words it carries
